blocks.en: 1. The Walk to Emmaus
blocks.es_reference: 1. El camino a Emaús

blocks.en: On the afternoon of the first Easter, two of His disciples were walking the seven miles from Jerusalem to a village called Emmaus. They were heartbroken. They had hoped Jesus was the One to redeem Israel. Now He was dead, His body was missing, and rumors were swirling. A Stranger joined them on the road and asked what they were talking about. They told Him — without recognizing Him. And then Luke records the most important hermeneutics lesson ever given:
blocks.es_reference: La tarde del primer domingo de resurrección, dos de Sus discípulos caminaban las siete millas de Jerusalén a una aldea llamada Emaús. Iban con el corazón quebrantado. Habían esperado que Jesús fuera el que había de redimir a Israel. Ahora estaba muerto, Su cuerpo había desaparecido, y los rumores corrían. Un Forastero se les unió en el camino y les preguntó de qué hablaban. Se lo contaron — sin reconocerlo. Y luego Lucas registra la lección de hermenéutica más importante jamás dada:

blocks.en: “And beginning at Moses and all the Prophets, He expounded to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning Himself.” (Luke 24:27, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: «Y comenzando desde Moisés, y siguiendo por todos los profetas, les declaraba en todas las Escrituras lo que de Él decían.» (Lucas 24:27, RVG)

blocks.en: The risen Christ’s first sermon was an exegesis class. Not a victory speech. Not a doctrinal lecture. He walked them through the whole Old Testament — Moses, the Prophets, every Scripture — and showed how the parts speak to each other and to Himself. That is what we mean by Scripture interprets Scripture.
blocks.es_reference: El primer sermón de Cristo resucitado fue una clase de exégesis. No fue un discurso de victoria. No fue una conferencia doctrinal. Los recorrió por todo el Antiguo Testamento — Moisés, los Profetas, todas las Escrituras — y les mostró cómo las partes se hablan entre sí y hablan de Él. A eso nos referimos cuando decimos que la Escritura interpreta a la Escritura.

blocks.en: 2. The Bible Is One Book
blocks.es_reference: 2. La Biblia es un solo libro

blocks.en: Sixty-six books. Approximately forty authors. Three languages. Roughly sixteen centuries of writing. One Author behind it all. The Bible is among the very few books in human history written across that scale with this kind of coherence. The doctrine of canonical unity says that because one Spirit inspired every word, the parts of the Bible are not strangers to each other. They are family. Each one knows the others. Genesis was written so Revelation could rest on it. Revelation was written so Genesis could be completed. Every passage in the middle holds the two ends together.
blocks.es_reference: Sesenta y seis libros. Aproximadamente cuarenta autores. Tres idiomas. Unos dieciséis siglos de escritura. Un solo Autor detrás de todo. La Biblia está entre los pocos libros en la historia humana escritos a esa escala con esta clase de coherencia. La doctrina de la unidad canónica dice que, porque un solo Espíritu inspiró cada palabra, las partes de la Biblia no son extrañas entre sí. Son familia. Cada una conoce a las otras. Génesis fue escrito para que Apocalipsis pudiera descansar sobre él. Apocalipsis fue escrito para que Génesis pudiera completarse. Cada pasaje en medio sostiene los dos extremos.

blocks.en: This is why no verse of the Bible can be safely interpreted in isolation. A verse without its book is a sentence without a paragraph. A book without the canon is a paragraph without a chapter. The whole Bible is the chapter, and every interpretive question must ultimately be brought to the whole.
blocks.es_reference: Por eso ningún versículo de la Biblia puede interpretarse con seguridad de manera aislada. Un versículo sin su libro es una oración sin un párrafo. Un libro sin el canon es un párrafo sin un capítulo. La Biblia entera es el capítulo, y cada pregunta interpretativa debe finalmente ser llevada al todo.

blocks.en: 3. Jesus Himself the First Exegete
blocks.es_reference: 3. Jesús mismo, el primer exégeta

blocks.en: Luke 24:27 is not the only place we see this principle in action; it is the place we see it modeled by the Lord Himself. He could have proved His resurrection by appearing in the temple court at noon. He chose instead to walk seven miles with two grieving men and open the Scriptures to them. Whatever else hermeneutics is, it is the discipline our risen Lord considered worth investing His first Easter afternoon in.
blocks.es_reference: Lucas 24:27 no es el único lugar donde vemos este principio en acción; es el lugar donde lo vemos modelado por el Señor mismo. Podría haber probado Su resurrección apareciendo en el atrio del templo al mediodía. Eligió en cambio caminar siete millas con dos hombres afligidos y abrirles las Escrituras. Cualquier otra cosa que sea la hermenéutica, es la disciplina en la cual nuestro Señor resucitado consideró que valía la pena invertir Su primera tarde de resurrección.

blocks.en: Later that same evening Jesus appeared to the eleven and did the same thing again:
blocks.es_reference: Esa misma tarde, más tarde, Jesús se apareció a los once e hizo lo mismo otra vez:

blocks.en: “These are the words which I spoke to you while I was still with you, that all things must be fulfilled which were written in the Law of Moses and the Prophets and the Psalms concerning Me. And He opened their understanding, that they might comprehend the Scriptures.” (Luke 24:44–45, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: «Estas son las palabras que os hablé, estando aún con vosotros: que era necesario que se cumpliesen todas las cosas que están escritas de mí en la ley de Moisés, y en los profetas, y en los salmos. Entonces les abrió el entendimiento, para que comprendiesen las Escrituras.» (Lucas 24:44–45, RVG)

blocks.en: Notice the three divisions: the Law of Moses, the Prophets, the Psalms. That is how the Jews divided the Hebrew Scriptures. Jesus is saying, in effect: The whole Old Testament has been about Me. Every section. Read it through that lens and it opens.
blocks.es_reference: Note las tres divisiones: la Ley de Moisés, los Profetas, los Salmos. Así dividían los judíos las Escrituras hebreas. Jesús está diciendo, en efecto: todo el Antiguo Testamento ha tratado de Mí. Cada sección. Léalo a través de ese lente y se abre.

blocks.en: 4. The Three-Fold Cord
blocks.es_reference: 4. El cordón de tres dobleces

blocks.en: In practice, the principle of Scripture-interprets-Scripture operates on three levels at once. Think of it as a three-fold cord that holds each verse in place.
blocks.es_reference: En la práctica, el principio de que la Escritura interpreta a la Escritura opera en tres niveles a la vez. Piénselo como un cordón de tres dobleces que sostiene cada versículo en su lugar.

blocks.en: First, clear passages illuminate difficult ones. The Bible says some things plainly and some things obscurely. The wise pastor anchors his interpretation in the plain places and lets them light up the dark ones. If a single difficult verse seems to teach what twenty clear verses deny, the difficult verse must mean something other than what it appears to say. Build doctrine from the daylight, not from the shadows.
blocks.es_reference: Primero, los pasajes claros iluminan los difíciles. La Biblia dice algunas cosas claramente y otras oscuramente. El pastor sabio ancla su interpretación en los lugares claros y deja que iluminen los oscuros. Si un solo versículo difícil parece enseñar lo que veinte versículos claros niegan, el versículo difícil debe significar algo distinto de lo que parece decir. Edifique la doctrina desde la luz del día, no desde las sombras.

blocks.en: Second, repeated teaching outweighs isolated mention. A doctrine the Bible repeats fifty times is more important than a phrase it uses once. The early church creeds were built on what Scripture says often and emphatically, not on what it says obscurely and in passing. A pastor who builds his doctrine on a single verse is building on a single nail. A pastor who builds on a repeated teaching is building on a beam.
blocks.es_reference: Segundo, la enseñanza repetida pesa más que la mención aislada. Una doctrina que la Biblia repite cincuenta veces es más importante que una frase que usa una sola vez. Los credos de la iglesia primitiva se edificaron sobre lo que la Escritura dice a menudo y enfáticamente, no sobre lo que dice oscuramente y de paso. Un pastor que edifica su doctrina sobre un solo versículo está edificando sobre un solo clavo. Un pastor que edifica sobre una enseñanza repetida está edificando sobre una viga.

blocks.en: Third, the whole canon holds each verse in place. We saw this in our third unit when Satan misquoted Psalm 91 and Jesus answered with Deuteronomy 6. We saw it again in our fourth unit when the whole book of Esther turned on Genesis 12:3, the covenant promise to Abraham. Every verse sits inside the canon, and the canon holds it where God put it.
blocks.es_reference: Tercero, el canon entero sostiene cada versículo en su lugar. Vimos esto en nuestra tercera unidad cuando Satanás citó mal el Salmo 91 y Jesús respondió con Deuteronomio 6. Lo vimos otra vez en nuestra cuarta unidad cuando el libro entero de Ester giraba sobre Génesis 12:3, la promesa del pacto a Abraham. Cada versículo está dentro del canon, y el canon lo sostiene donde Dios lo puso.

blocks.en: 5. A Worked Example — Philippians 4:13
blocks.es_reference: 5. Un ejemplo trabajado: Filipenses 4:13

blocks.en: Take the most-quoted verse on locker-room walls and athlete tattoos: I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me. The verse is real. The translation is fair. But what does it mean? Pulled out alone, it sounds like a divine power-up — whatever I attempt, Christ will make me succeed.
blocks.es_reference: Tome el versículo más citado en las paredes de los vestuarios y en los tatuajes de los atletas: todo lo puedo en Cristo que me fortalece. El versículo es real. La traducción es justa. Pero ¿qué significa? Sacado solo, suena como un impulso de poder divino — cualquier cosa que intente, Cristo me hará triunfar.

blocks.en: Now apply Scripture interprets Scripture. Back up two verses. Paul writes: I have learned, in whatever state I am, to be content. I know how to be abased, and I know how to abound. Everywhere and in all things I have learned both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need. Then comes verse 13: I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.
blocks.es_reference: Ahora aplique la Escritura interpreta a la Escritura. Retroceda dos versículos. Pablo escribe: he aprendido a contentarme cualquiera que sea mi situación. Sé estar humillado, y sé tener abundancia; en todo y por todo estoy enseñado, así para estar saciado como para tener hambre, así para tener abundancia como para padecer necesidad. Entonces viene el versículo 13: todo lo puedo en Cristo que me fortalece.

blocks.en: The “all things” Paul can do is not any goal I dream up. It is be content in plenty and in want, in success and in failure, in fullness and in hunger. Christ does not promise the believer victory at every venture. He promises the believer contentment in every circumstance. Read the verse with its paragraph and a prosperity-gospel reading dies on the page. Read the verse without its paragraph and a generation of athletes learns to expect the wrong thing from God.
blocks.es_reference: El «todo» que Pablo puede hacer no es cualquier meta que yo sueñe. Es contentarme en abundancia y en escasez, en éxito y en fracaso, saciado y con hambre. Cristo no le promete al creyente la victoria en cada empresa. Le promete al creyente el contentamiento en cada circunstancia. Lea el versículo con su párrafo y una lectura del evangelio de la prosperidad muere en la página. Lea el versículo sin su párrafo y toda una generación de atletas aprende a esperar lo equivocado de Dios.

blocks.en: 6. The Actor Who Memorized Mark
blocks.es_reference: 6. El actor que memorizó a Marcos

blocks.en: Eric Booth was a New York stage actor. The British actor Alec McCowen had built a one-man show in which he recited the entire Gospel of Mark from memory. Booth was cast to do the same in a three-week run in Chicago. He came to the job, by his own admission, as a secular man with no ax to grind. He simply had to learn the lines. He started memorizing them — just plain hard work, very little emotional response. But then the work began to do its own work on him. He later said: I have this gut-level feeling that all these things happened. I don’t know how, and I don’t understand it, but now somehow I believe it all took place just as it was described. And so I live with something beyond my understanding. An actor preparing for a role became a Christian by saturation in Scripture.
blocks.es_reference: Eric Booth era un actor de teatro neoyorquino. El actor británico Alec McCowen había creado una obra unipersonal en la cual recitaba de memoria el Evangelio de Marcos completo. Booth fue contratado para hacer lo mismo en una temporada de tres semanas en Chicago. Llegó al trabajo, según él mismo admitió, como un hombre secular sin hacha que afilar. Simplemente tenía que aprender las líneas. Comenzó a memorizarlas — trabajo duro sin más, muy poca respuesta emocional. Pero luego el trabajo comenzó a hacer su propia obra en él. Dijo después: tengo esta sensación visceral de que todas estas cosas sucedieron. No sé cómo, y no lo entiendo, pero ahora de alguna manera creo que todo ocurrió tal como fue descrito. Y así vivo con algo más allá de mi entendimiento. Un actor que se preparaba para un papel se hizo cristiano por saturación en la Escritura.

blocks.en: That is what Scripture-interprets-Scripture does over time. It does not just inform the mind. It saturates the man. The pastor who lives inside the canon long enough begins to think in its categories, dream in its metaphors, see his church through its eyes. He no longer has to look up cross-references because the cross-references live in him. The Bible has interpreted him.
blocks.es_reference: Eso es lo que la Escritura-interpretando-a-la-Escritura hace con el tiempo. No solo informa la mente. Satura al hombre. El pastor que vive dentro del canon el tiempo suficiente comienza a pensar en sus categorías, a soñar en sus metáforas, a ver a su iglesia a través de sus ojos. Ya no tiene que buscar referencias cruzadas porque las referencias cruzadas viven en él. La Biblia lo ha interpretado a él.

blocks.en: 7. What This Principle Saves Us From
blocks.es_reference: 7. De qué nos salva este principio

blocks.en: The discipline of letting Scripture interpret Scripture saves the pastor from three serious errors that thrive in our day.
blocks.es_reference: La disciplina de dejar que la Escritura interprete a la Escritura salva al pastor de tres errores serios que prosperan en nuestros días.

blocks.en: It saves him from single-verse cults. Almost every modern cult is built on one isolated verse used to override the rest of the Bible. Jehovah’s Witnesses build the denial of Christ’s deity on a strained reading of John 1:1, ignoring John 1:14, John 20:28, Hebrews 1:8, Titus 2:13, and a hundred other passages that say what John 1:1 says. The cure for the cult is never to abandon the Bible. The cure is to bring the cult’s favorite verse to the rest of the Bible — and let the canon hold the verse in place.
blocks.es_reference: Lo salva de las sectas de un solo versículo. Casi toda secta moderna se edifica sobre un versículo aislado usado para anular el resto de la Biblia. Los Testigos de Jehová edifican la negación de la deidad de Cristo sobre una lectura forzada de Juan 1:1, ignorando Juan 1:14, Juan 20:28, Hebreos 1:8, Tito 2:13, y otros cien pasajes que dicen lo que dice Juan 1:1. La cura para la secta nunca es abandonar la Biblia. La cura es traer el versículo favorito de la secta al resto de la Biblia — y dejar que el canon sostenga el versículo en su lugar.

blocks.en: It saves him from chain-quoting — the bad habit of stringing together five verses from five different books that share a single word but not a single meaning. A pastor can “prove” almost anything that way: take the word fire in Exodus 3, Acts 2, and Hebrews 12, treat them as if they teach the same thing, and you have a sermon. You also have a misreading of three different passages. Scripture interprets Scripture means more than sharing vocabulary; it means sharing context, argument, and theology.
blocks.es_reference: Lo salva de la cadena de citas — el mal hábito de hilar cinco versículos de cinco libros distintos que comparten una sola palabra pero no un solo significado. Un pastor puede «probar» casi cualquier cosa así: tome la palabra fuego en Éxodo 3, Hechos 2, y Hebreos 12, trátelos como si enseñaran lo mismo, y tendrá un sermón. También tendrá una mala lectura de tres pasajes distintos. La Escritura interpretando a la Escritura significa más que compartir vocabulario; significa compartir contexto, argumento, y teología.

blocks.en: It saves him from isolated proof-texting. Even when a verse is quoted accurately, in its right context, on its own meaning, the pastor is still wise to ask what other Scripture stands behind it and beside it. A single verse can be misunderstood by an honest reader; a verse held in the company of its fellows almost cannot.
blocks.es_reference: Lo salva del uso aislado de versículos como prueba. Aun cuando un versículo se cite con precisión, en su contexto correcto, con su propio significado, el pastor todavía hace bien en preguntar qué otra Escritura está detrás de él y junto a él. Un solo versículo puede ser mal entendido por un lector honesto; un versículo sostenido en la compañía de sus compañeros casi no puede serlo.

blocks.en: 8. Did Not Our Heart Burn?
blocks.es_reference: 8. ¿No ardía nuestro corazón?

blocks.en: When Jesus left the two disciples at Emmaus, they did not say, What a clever Bible study that was. They said:
blocks.es_reference: Cuando Jesús dejó a los dos discípulos en Emaús, ellos no dijeron: qué estudio bíblico tan ingenioso fue ése. Dijeron:

blocks.en: “Did not our heart burn within us while He talked with us on the road, and while He opened the Scriptures to us?” (Luke 24:32, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: «¿No ardía nuestro corazón en nosotros, mientras nos hablaba en el camino, y cuando nos abría las Escrituras?» (Lucas 24:32, RVG)

blocks.en: That is the payoff of Scripture-interprets-Scripture. Not better lecture notes. Not a more impressive doctrinal statement. A burning heart. When the parts of the Bible begin to speak to each other in front of the pastor, and through him in front of his people, the result is a fire that no academic exercise can produce. The Word that was given by the Spirit is opened by the Spirit and warms the people of the Spirit.
blocks.es_reference: Ése es el resultado de la Escritura-interpretando-a-la-Escritura. No mejores apuntes de conferencia. No una declaración doctrinal más impresionante. Un corazón ardiente. Cuando las partes de la Biblia comienzan a hablarse entre sí delante del pastor, y por medio de él delante de su pueblo, el resultado es un fuego que ningún ejercicio académico puede producir. La Palabra que fue dada por el Espíritu es abierta por el Espíritu y calienta al pueblo del Espíritu.

blocks.en: If your sermons leave your hearers informed but unwarmed, the issue is rarely your delivery. The issue is usually that the parts of the Bible have not yet been allowed to speak to each other in your study. Let them speak. Sit with two passages until you see how they hold each other. The burn comes when the connections come.
blocks.es_reference: Si sus sermones dejan a sus oyentes informados pero no calentados, el problema rara vez es su entrega. El problema es generalmente que las partes de la Biblia no han sido dejadas todavía hablarse entre sí en su estudio. Déjelas hablar. Siéntese con dos pasajes hasta ver cómo se sostienen una a la otra. El ardor viene cuando llegan las conexiones.

blocks.en: 9. Practical Steps
blocks.es_reference: 9. Pasos prácticos

blocks.en: Three habits will form a pastor who lets Scripture interpret Scripture. Cross-references. A study Bible lists the parallel passages in the margin. When you study a verse, look up every reference and read it in its own context. Do not just glance; read the paragraph each reference sits in. Half an hour of cross-referencing will teach you more than half a day of reading commentaries about a verse.
blocks.es_reference: Tres hábitos formarán a un pastor que deja que la Escritura interprete a la Escritura. Las referencias cruzadas. Una Biblia de estudio enumera los pasajes paralelos en el margen. Cuando estudie un versículo, busque cada referencia y léala en su propio contexto. No solo le eche un vistazo; lea el párrafo en el cual cada referencia se encuentra. Media hora de referencias cruzadas le enseñará más que medio día de leer comentarios sobre un versículo.

blocks.en: Concordance work. When a word matters to your text, look it up in a concordance and read every occurrence the Bible gives. A word does not necessarily mean the same thing in every passage — that is where context still rules — but tracing a word teaches you the range of meanings God has given it. Faith, righteousness, justify, flesh, spirit, world — almost every important biblical word carries shades the pastor needs to know.
blocks.es_reference: El trabajo con concordancia. Cuando una palabra importa para su texto, búsquela en una concordancia y lea cada vez que aparece en la Biblia. Una palabra no necesariamente significa lo mismo en cada pasaje — ahí sigue gobernando el contexto — pero rastrear una palabra le enseña el rango de significados que Dios le ha dado. Fe, justicia, justificar, carne, espíritu, mundo — casi cada palabra bíblica importante carga matices que el pastor necesita conocer.

blocks.en: Whole-Bible reading. The pastor who has never read the whole Bible through cannot let Scripture interpret Scripture, because he does not yet know what Scripture says. Read it through every year if you can. Read it slowly — not as a chore, but as a relationship. The cross-references you cannot look up will rise unbidden when you preach, because they live in you.
blocks.es_reference: La lectura de la Biblia entera. El pastor que nunca ha leído la Biblia entera no puede dejar que la Escritura interprete a la Escritura, porque todavía no sabe lo que la Escritura dice. Léala completa cada año si puede. Léala despacio — no como una tarea, sino como una relación. Las referencias cruzadas que no podrá buscar surgirán sin invitación cuando predique, porque viven en usted.

blocks.en: 10. Preach What Burns
blocks.es_reference: 10. Predique lo que arde

blocks.en: The two disciples did not stay at the Emmaus inn after Jesus left them. Luke says they got up that same hour and walked the seven miles back to Jerusalem in the dark, to tell the others. A burning heart cannot be kept indoors. When the Word has burned in the pastor’s study, his Sunday is not a duty. It is a delivery.
blocks.es_reference: Los dos discípulos no se quedaron en la posada de Emaús después de que Jesús los dejó. Lucas dice que se levantaron esa misma hora y caminaron las siete millas de regreso a Jerusalén en la oscuridad, para contárselo a los otros. Un corazón ardiente no puede quedarse encerrado en casa. Cuando la Palabra ha ardido en el estudio del pastor, su domingo no es un deber. Es una entrega.

blocks.en: Preach what burns. Preach what holds together. Preach what the canon has hammered into one shape. When Scripture interprets Scripture in your study, you do not need to invent enthusiasm in the pulpit. The fire is already there. Your job is only to bring it down to your people without smothering it on the way.
blocks.es_reference: Predique lo que arde. Predique lo que se sostiene unido. Predique lo que el canon ha martillado en una sola forma. Cuando la Escritura interpreta a la Escritura en su estudio, no necesita inventar entusiasmo en el púlpito. El fuego ya está ahí. Su tarea es solamente llevarlo a su pueblo sin sofocarlo en el camino.

mc.stem: The Bible passage that most clearly models "Scripture interprets Scripture" being done by Jesus Himself is:
options: The Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5-7)
The cleansing of the temple (John 2)
The road to Emmaus (Luke 24:27)
The wedding at Cana (John 2:1-11)
mc.why: Correct. On the road to Emmaus the risen Christ walked two disciples through Moses, the Prophets, and "all the Scriptures" to show them what every part of the Old Testament said about Him. That is canonical exegesis modeled by the Lord Himself.

mc.stem: According to Luke 24:44, what three divisions did Jesus name when He said the whole Old Testament spoke of Him?
options: Pentateuch, History, Wisdom
The Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms
The Apocrypha, the Septuagint, the Targums
Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus
mc.why: Correct. Those were the three traditional Jewish divisions of the Hebrew Bible. Jesus said the whole Old Testament — every section — had been about Him. Read through that lens, the canon opens.

mc.stem: The doctrine of canonical unity teaches that:
options: Only the New Testament should govern Christian doctrine
The Bible is mostly contradictions reconciled by clever theologians
The Bible's sixty-six books were inspired by one Spirit and form one coherent message
Each Bible book stands entirely on its own
mc.why: Correct. Approximately forty authors, three languages, roughly sixteen centuries, one Author behind it all. Because one Spirit inspired every word, the parts of the Bible are not strangers to each other — they are family.

mc.stem: The first level of the "three-fold cord" of Scripture-interprets-Scripture is:
options: Clear passages illuminate difficult ones
The original Hebrew is always preferred to the Greek
Newer revelation always cancels older revelation
Personal experience completes Scripture
mc.why: Correct. The wise pastor anchors his interpretation in the plain places and lets them light up the dark ones. If a difficult verse seems to teach what twenty clear verses deny, the difficult verse must mean something other than what it appears to say.

mc.stem: The second level of the three-fold cord is:
options: Sentimental verses outweigh practical ones
Old Testament verses outweigh New Testament ones
Famous verses outweigh obscure ones
Repeated teaching outweighs isolated mention
mc.why: Correct. A doctrine the Bible repeats fifty times is more important than a phrase it uses once. A pastor who builds doctrine on a single verse is building on a single nail; a pastor who builds on a repeated teaching is building on a beam.

mc.stem: The third level of the three-fold cord is:
options: Each pastor's denomination decides the meaning
Modern theologians correct ancient ones
The whole canon holds each verse in place
Whoever shouts loudest wins the debate
mc.why: Correct. Every verse sits inside the canon, and the canon holds it where God put it. We saw this in Unit 3 (Jesus answering Psalm 91 with Deuteronomy 6) and Unit 4 (Esther driven by Genesis 12). The whole Bible holds each verse.

mc.stem: The lesson uses Philippians 4:13 ("I can do all things through Christ") as a worked example of:
options: A verse so clear no context is needed
A verse whose meaning is restored by reading verses 11-12 with it
A verse meant only for first-century Christians
A verse that has no application today
mc.why: Correct. Verses 11-12 are about contentment in plenty and in want. Verse 13's "all things" is therefore being content in every circumstance — not a divine guarantee of every venture's success. Scripture interprets Scripture, and the prosperity reading dies.

mc.stem: When read with Philippians 4:11-12, what does "I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me" actually mean?
options: Christ guarantees success in any venture I attempt
I will be physically protected from all harm
I will become a great athlete or businessman
I can be content in every circumstance — plenty and want, success and failure
mc.why: Correct. Paul's context is contentment: "I have learned, in whatever state I am, to be content. I know how to be abased, and how to abound." The "all things" is contentment in every circumstance, not victory in every venture.

mc.stem: The Eric Booth story (the New York actor) illustrates:
options: How dramatic recital improves Bible translation
How memorizing Scripture in large amounts can transform a secular man into a believer
How professional acting techniques should be used in preaching
How Mark's Gospel is the easiest to memorize
mc.why: Correct. Booth came to the work as a secular man with no ax to grind. He simply memorized the lines. By the time he finished, he believed. Scripture in saturation does its own work — the Bible interprets the man who lives inside it.

mc.stem: The lesson identifies three serious errors that the principle "Scripture interprets Scripture" saves the pastor from. The first of these is:
options: Excessive use of cross-references
Single-verse cults — building error on one isolated passage
Ignoring the New Testament
Reading too many commentaries
mc.why: Correct. Almost every modern cult builds on one isolated verse used to override the rest of the Bible. Jehovah's Witnesses lean on a strained reading of John 1:1 while ignoring John 1:14, John 20:28, Hebrews 1:8, Titus 2:13, and many more.

mc.stem: The second error this principle saves the pastor from is:
options: Chain-quoting — stringing together verses that share a single word but not a single meaning
Praying too long before sermons
Memorizing too much Scripture
Studying Greek and Hebrew
mc.why: Correct. A pastor can "prove" almost anything by stringing verses that share vocabulary but not meaning. The word fire in Exodus 3, Acts 2, and Hebrews 12 carries different theological weights — chain-quoting collapses them and produces misreadings.

mc.stem: The third error this principle saves the pastor from is:
options: Preaching too long
Using study Bibles
Isolated proof-texting — quoting a verse without asking what other Scripture stands behind and beside it
Quoting from memory
mc.why: Correct. Even an accurately quoted verse, in its proper context, with its right meaning, is wise to set in the company of other Scripture. A verse held by its fellows almost cannot be misunderstood; a verse standing alone often can be.

mc.stem: The lesson identifies a Jehovah's Witness use of John 1:1 as an example of:
options: A single-verse cult building error on one isolated passage
A legitimate alternative reading
Greek scholarship at its finest
A successful exegetical tradition
mc.why: Correct. The JW denial of Christ's deity hangs on a strained reading of John 1:1 while ignoring John 1:14, John 20:28, Hebrews 1:8, Titus 2:13, and dozens of other passages that affirm what John 1:1 plainly says. Single-verse cult.

mc.stem: The famous response of the two Emmaus disciples after Jesus opened the Scriptures to them was:
options: "What a clever Bible study that was"
"We need to write this down for the church"
"Did not our heart burn within us?"
"How can these things be?"
mc.why: Correct (Luke 24:32). The payoff of Scripture interprets Scripture is not better lecture notes or a more impressive doctrinal statement. It is a burning heart. When the parts begin to speak to each other, fire follows.

mc.stem: According to the lesson, if a pastor's sermons leave hearers "informed but unwarmed," the usual issue is:
options: The parts of the Bible have not yet been allowed to speak to each other in his study
The translation is wrong
The congregation is too small
The pastor needs a better microphone
mc.why: Correct. The problem is rarely delivery. The problem is usually that the canonical connections have not yet been made in the pastor's study. Sit with two passages until you see how they hold each other. The burn comes when the connections come.

mc.stem: The lesson recommends three practical habits for a pastor who lets Scripture interpret Scripture. The first habit is:
options: Listening to many sermons each week
Watching Christian television
Joining several denominations
Cross-referencing — looking up the parallel passages your study Bible lists in the margin
mc.why: Correct. Look up every reference, read it in its own paragraph. Half an hour of cross-referencing teaches more than half a day of reading commentaries about a verse. The parallels train your eye to see how the Bible speaks to itself.

mc.stem: The second practical habit the lesson recommends is:
options: Memorizing the entire Bible by age forty
Concordance work — looking up every occurrence of a word that matters to your text
Visiting Israel every year
Avoiding all Bible study guides
mc.why: Correct. Tracing a word through every appearance teaches the range of meanings God has given it. Faith, righteousness, justify, flesh, spirit, world — almost every important biblical word carries shades a pastor needs to know.

mc.stem: The third practical habit the lesson recommends is:
options: Whole-Bible reading — reading the Bible through every year if possible
Speed-reading on Sunday afternoons
Reading only the New Testament
Reading only with commentaries
mc.why: Correct. A pastor who has never read the whole Bible through cannot let Scripture interpret Scripture, because he does not yet know what Scripture says. Read it through every year. The cross-references you cannot look up will rise unbidden in your preaching.

mc.stem: According to the lesson, what did the Emmaus disciples do immediately after Jesus revealed Himself and disappeared?
options: They went to bed for the night, planning to tell the others in the morning
They wrote a written account of what had happened
They began to argue about what they had just seen
They got up that same hour and walked the seven miles back to Jerusalem in the dark
mc.why: Correct. A burning heart cannot be kept indoors. They walked back through the night to tell the others. When the Word has burned in the pastor's study, his Sunday is not a duty — it is a delivery he cannot wait to make.

mc.stem: The closing charge of this unit is:
options: Memorize at least ten verses each week
Read only the New Testament
Avoid all cross-referencing
Preach what burns — what the canon has hammered into one shape
mc.why: Correct. Preach what burns. Preach what holds together. When Scripture interprets Scripture in the study, the pastor does not need to manufacture enthusiasm in the pulpit. The fire is already there; his job is only to bring it down without smothering it.

fill.prompt: On the first Easter afternoon, two disciples were walking the seven miles from Jerusalem to a village called ____.
"And beginning at ____ and all the Prophets, He expounded to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning Himself." (Luke 24:27)
The doctrine of canonical ____ says that because one Spirit inspired every word, the parts of the Bible are not strangers to each other.
In Luke 24:44 Jesus names the three divisions of the Hebrew Scriptures: the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the ____.
Because clear passages illuminate difficult ones, the pastor should build doctrine from the daylight, not from the ____.
A pastor who builds his doctrine on a single verse is building on a single ____; one who builds on a repeated teaching is building on a beam.

Read with the verses around it about being content in plenty and in want, Philippians 4:13 shows that Christ does not promise the believer victory at every venture; He promises ____ in every circumstance.
The actor Eric Booth, who memorized the entire Gospel of ____ for a one-man show, became a Christian by saturation in Scripture.
The bad habit of stringing together verses from different books that share a single word but not a single meaning is called ____.
"Did not our heart ____ within us while He talked with us on the road, and while He opened the Scriptures to us?" (Luke 24:32)

sa.prompt: Tell the Emmaus-road story (Luke 24:13-32) and explain why this lesson calls it the most important hermeneutics lesson ever given.
sa.model: On the first Easter two heartbroken disciples walked the road to Emmaus, and a Stranger — the risen Jesus — joined them. Beginning at Moses and all the Prophets, He expounded in all the Scriptures the things concerning Himself. The lesson calls this the most important hermeneutics lesson ever given because Jesus shows that all of Scripture points to Him.

sa.prompt: Explain the doctrine of canonical unity and why it grounds the principle "Scripture interprets Scripture."
sa.model: Canonical unity means that though the Bible's many books were written by dozens of human authors across centuries, one divine Author — the Holy Spirit — inspired them all, giving the whole a single coherent message. Because the sixty-six books form one unified book, a clear passage in one place may be used to interpret a difficult one in another. The unity grounds the principle that Scripture interprets Scripture.

sa.prompt: Describe the three-fold cord that holds each verse in place. Name and explain each of its three strands.
sa.model: The three-fold cord holds each verse with three strands. First, clear passages illumine the difficult ones. Second, a truth repeated across many texts outweighs a meaning drawn from a single obscure verse. Third, the whole canon surrounds and anchors each verse. Together the three strands keep any one verse from being pulled out of place.

sa.prompt: Take Philippians 4:13 as your worked example. Show how reading verses 11-12 with it transforms the meaning and refutes the prosperity-gospel reading.
sa.model: Philippians 4:13 — 'I can do all things through Christ' — is not a promise of achievement or wealth. Read with verses 11-12, Paul has learned to be content whether abased or abounding, in want or in plenty. The 'all things' is enduring every circumstance through Christ's strength, which refutes the prosperity reading.

sa.prompt: Tell the Eric Booth story (the New York actor memorizing Mark's Gospel) and explain what it teaches about Scripture's transforming power when read in saturation.
sa.model: Eric Booth was a secular New York actor cast to recite the whole Gospel of Mark from memory, with no ax to grind. As he memorized the lines, the work began to do its own work on him, and the saturated Word brought the unbelieving actor to faith. The story shows Scripture's transforming power when it is taken in by saturation.

sa.prompt: Name the three errors that the principle of Scripture-interprets-Scripture saves the pastor from, and briefly describe each.
sa.model: The principle saves the pastor from three errors: building doctrine on a single isolated verse; the cult habit of chain-quoting verses out of context to prove a system; and proof-texting that ignores everything the rest of the canon says. Letting Scripture interpret Scripture keeps no verse standing alone.

sa.prompt: Explain how a single-verse cult (such as the Jehovah's Witness use of John 1:1) is corrected by the principle of Scripture-interprets-Scripture.
sa.model: A single-verse cult like the Jehovah's Witnesses leans on John 1:1, rendering it 'the Word was a god' to deny Christ's deity. The principle corrects this by reading the verse against the whole canon: the many passages that affirm Christ as God cannot be ignored or contradicted by one disputed translation. Scripture interpreting Scripture protects His deity.

sa.prompt: Discuss Luke 24:32 — "Did not our heart burn within us?" — and explain why this verse describes the true payoff of Scripture-interprets-Scripture.
sa.model: On the Emmaus road the disciples asked, 'Did not our heart burn within us while He opened the Scriptures to us?' That burning heart is the payoff of Scripture-interpreting-Scripture — not better lecture notes but a fire the Spirit lights when the parts of the Bible speak to each other. The Word given by the Spirit is opened by the Spirit and warms the people of the Spirit.

sa.prompt: Name the three practical habits this lesson recommends for forming a pastor who lets Scripture interpret Scripture, and briefly explain each.
sa.model: The lesson recommends three habits: use cross-references to let one text point to another, keep a concordance to trace a word across the canon, and make the regular reading of the whole Bible a habit so its parts live together in your mind. These habits form a pastor who lets Scripture interpret Scripture by comparing text with text.

sa.prompt: Explain what it means that "the Bible interprets the man who lives inside it" and why this connects Scripture-interprets-Scripture to the pastor's own transformation.
sa.model: When a pastor lives inside the Bible long enough, the Bible begins to interpret him: its saturation transforms his thinking until his categories and metaphors become biblical ones. This connects Scripture-interprets-Scripture to the pastor's own transformation — the Word he interprets all week ends up interpreting and reshaping the man himself.
